target_customer: English language manga readers who pay about $4.99 a month, plus free ad supported readers
problem: Fans wanted legal, affordable, global access to many licensed manga series in one place. Azuki offers a Netflix style subscription of officially licensed titles.
business_model: consumer subscription plus ads on a free tier

founders.name: Abbas Jaffery
founders.background_notes: YC page: previously worked in community management, QA, backend engineering and product management; employers not named.

founders.name: Adela Chang
founders.background_notes: Senior mobile developer at those companies per the YC page.

founders.name: Evan Minto
founders.background_notes: Leads design, marketing and content acquisition; later titled Licensing and Marketing Director.

founders.name: Krystyn Neisess
founders.background_notes: Android development and social media per YC page.

founders.name: Ken Urata
founders.background_notes: Software engineer and English to Japanese translator per YC page.

competitors.name: Shonen Jump Vault (Viz Media)
competitors.what: manga subscription limited to North America

competitors.name: Manga Plus (Shueisha)
competitors.what: global manga reader with a higher buy in price than Azuki

technical_complexity.rationale: Web, iOS and Android readers with a subscription backend are standard engineering; the hard part is licensing content, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Licensing deals with Kodansha and indie publishers are the main asset but are non exclusive and open to larger rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Publisher apps were already offering subscriptions at launch. No acquisition found; Azuki rebranded as Omoi in November 2025.

market_need_then: Launch coverage in June 2021 describes demand for a global all you can read manga service, with over 170 Kodansha series at launch for about $5 a month.

branding.name_origin: Azuki is the Japanese red bean; the launch tweet joked 'yes, we are a bean' but no source states the reason. Omoi is a Japanese word loosely meaning thought, feeling or emotion.
branding.domain_note: Azuki used azuki.co; the 2025 rebrand moved the web platform to omoi.com.

identity.logo: New logo and colour scheme introduced with the 2025 rebrand; design not described in sources.
identity.voice_and_tone: Approachable and trustworthy, centered on officially licensed manga.

branding.brand_signature: Playful bean joke in launch messaging

rebrands.why: Co-founder Evan Minto said the name reduced confusion with other companies using Azuki and fit a broader creative mission.

branding.community_and_virality: Comics Beat says the platform built a loyal following through indie publisher partnerships and an ad free subscription.

brand_strength.rationale: Reader survey shows 7.1 percent usage versus 35.9 percent for Manga Plus, and the founders later said the Azuki name was confusable with unrelated companies.

outcome_analysis: Azuki launched in June 2021 with Kodansha titles and joined YC in Winter 2022 with a $500K investment. It stayed small with licensing dependence on publishers and competition from Manga Plus and Viz, then rebranded as Omoi in November 2025 partly because the name was shared by unrelated companies. It remains active with a catalog above 500 titles.
notes: PitchBook lists KiraKira Media at $750K total with Goodwater Capital, VCBacked lists $665K; Caplight shows implausible figures. Not recorded as rounds. The YC investment stage is 'other' because sources call it an investment, not a priced round. The YC page lists five founders although team size is 3. Reader survey date unknown. The brand effect is a judgment based on the founders' own rebrand explanation.
